Usage:
  pqax check <file> [--part <name>]   Validate a PQAX file, or the footprint inside a VPAX file.
  pqax info <file> [--part <name>]    Show the format, the collection, the parts, and the rows of each table.
  pqax collect --local <folder> --output <file>     Collect a footprint from a folder in the OneLake layout.
  pqax collect --workspace <id> --item <name> --output <file>   Collect from OneLake, with a device-code sign-in. See pqax collect --help.
  pqax --version                      Show the version.

A file with the extension .vpax, or any file with --part, is read as a VPAX file that holds the
footprint as a part, Footprint.pqax unless --part names another one.

Exit codes: 0 valid or done, 1 invalid, 2 wrong command line or file that cannot be read.

result.stdout:
Usage:
  pqax collect --local <folder> --output <file.pqax> [--item <name.Kind>]... [options]
  pqax collect --workspace <name or id> --item <name.Kind> [--item ...] --output <file.pqax> [--tenant <id>] [--browser] [options]

--local reads a folder with the OneLake layout: <item>.<Kind>/Tables/[<schema>/]<table>. Without --item, every
lakehouse, warehouse, mirrored database, and SQL database in the folder. --workspace reads OneLake after a sign-in
with a device code, which the command prints, or in the browser with --browser; an item is named as in OneLake,
such as Sales.Lakehouse.
Name the workspace and the items both by name or both by id: OneLake refuses a workspace id with item names.

Options:
  --depth summary|files|rowGroups|columnChunks   The detail kept for each table. Default columnChunks.
  --level 1|2                                   1 reads the Delta logs, 2 also the Parquet footers. Default 2.
  --max-footers <n>                             Footers read for each table, 0 for all. Default 0.
  --max-commits <n>                             Commit files read for the history of each table; the commits the state needs are read anyway. Default 30.
  --parallelism <n>                             Storage requests at the same time. Default 16.
  --verbose                                     Print every OneLake request and its status code to the error output.

Exit codes: 0 written and valid, 1 written and invalid, 2 wrong command line or failure.
